steps.label: dprtc info surface and reported API version
steps.expect: zero exit; capture the full readable surface — version line answers dprtc.md unknown 4 (flib 2.3 vs restool 2.0-compatible header). No time or frequency should appear anywhere (DPRTC-I3: info success is not clock health)

steps.label: kernel PTP binding: fsl-dpaa2-ptp holds dprtc.0
steps.expect: zero exit; the driver symlink names fsl-dpaa2-ptp and a /dev/ptpN chardev exists — confirming the [read] kernel-ownership claim the reference environment never captured (DPRTC-I2's kernel side)

steps.label: device-tree ptp-timer node vs MC paddr
cmd: for d in /proc/device-tree/soc/*ptp*; do echo "$d"; hexdump -C "$d/reg" 2>/dev/null | head -3; done
steps.expect: capture the DT ptp-timer reg window (dprtc.md unknown 5). Only the DT half is observable — restool reads the MC attr's paddr/little_endian and silently discards both, so this records the DT side for the ledger and the unknown stays half-answered by design

steps.label: one-step-sync in each kernel dpni's tx timestamp modes
cmd: for n in /sys/bus/fsl-mc/drivers/fsl_dpaa2_eth/dpni.*/net/*; do ifn=$(basename "$n"); echo "== $ifn =="; ethtool -T "$ifn"; done
steps.expect: exit any; walk every kernel-bound dpni's netdev and read `ethtool -T`. ethtool may be absent — if so, say so and the surface stays unread this sitting. The oracle is whether 'Hardware Transmit Timestamp Modes' lists `onestep-sync`: its presence makes one-step 1588 claimable on this platform, its absence upholds the manual's two-step-only note (dprtc.md unknown 6)

steps.label: PTP clock capability surface
cmd: for f in /sys/class/ptp/ptp*/*; do [ -f "$f" ] && echo "$f=$(cat "$f" 2>/dev/null)"; done
steps.expect: exit any; dump every regular file under /sys/class/ptp/ptp*/ as path=value (n_alarms, n_ext_ts, n_per_out, pps_available, clock_name, max_adjustment, …). Records what the clock advertises for the one-step/SYNC path — the second observable feeding dprtc.md unknown 6
